#!/usr/bin/env python3
import csv
import pandas as pd

def main() -> None:
    """
    Reads the long‑format Eurostat data from outputs/t02_eurostat_raw.csv,
    pivots it into a wide matrix with one column per indicator,
    and writes the result to outputs/t11_city_indicator_matrix.csv.
    Missing values are written as empty cells (RFC 4180 compliant).
    """
    # Load the raw data
    df_raw = pd.read_csv("outputs/t02_eurostat_raw.csv")

    # Pivot: index is city_id, city_name, year – columns are indicator_id, values are the numeric value
    df_piv = df_raw.pivot(index=["city_id", "city_name", "year"],
                          columns="indicator_id",
                          values="value")

    # Reset the pivoted index to get a regular DataFrame
    df_piv = df_piv.reset_index()

    # Remove any remaining column level name introduced by pivot
    if df_piv.columns.name is not None:
        df_piv.columns.name = None

    # Determine the indicator columns (everything except the three identifier columns)
    identifier_cols = ("city_id", "city_name", "year")
    indicator_cols = [c for c in df_piv.columns if c not in identifier_cols]

    # Sort indicator columns for deterministic output order
    indicator_cols.sort()

    # Reorder DataFrame columns: identifiers first, then indicator columns in sorted order
    ordered_cols = list(identifier_cols) + indicator_cols
    df_piv = df_piv[ordered_cols]

    # Write the final matrix
    df_piv.to_csv("outputs/t11_city_indicator_matrix.csv",
                  index=False,
                  na_rep="",  # empty string for missing values
                  quoting=csv.QUOTE_MINIMAL)  # minimal quoting ensures RFC 4180 compliance

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
</solution_file>
